body:
## What happened

Any host command that recursively lists paths — \`bb.sdk.files.listPaths\`/\`listPathsRecursively\` under the hood — crashes on a workspace with a large enough file tree. In practice this shows up as an opaque \`HTTP 502\` from any caller (e.g. a plugin's \`listTree\` RPC), with no useful error surfaced to the user.

Repro: point a project/vault at a directory with roughly 100k+ files somewhere in its tree (a large Obsidian vault, a big monorepo, etc.) and call file listing/search on it.

## Root cause

\`apps/host-daemon/src/command-handlers/file-list.ts\`, \`listPathsRecursively\`, merges each subdirectory's results like this:

\`\`\`ts
results.push(
  ...(await listPathsRecursively({ ...args, dir: fullPath })),
);
\`\`\`

\`Array.prototype.push(...arr)\` spreads every element of \`arr\` onto the JS call stack as individual arguments. Once a subtree's accumulated result array crosses V8's argument-count ceiling (~100k, engine-dependent), this throws:

\`\`\`
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
\`\`\`

which propagates up as an unhandled error and surfaces to callers as a 502.

Minimal repro of the underlying JS behavior:

\`\`\`js
const results = [];
const big = new Array(200_000).fill(0).map((_, i) => ({ path: "x" + i }));
results.push(...big); // RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
\`\`\`

## Fix

Replace the spread-push with a plain loop (no argument-count limit). PR: #<!-- filled in below -->

Added a regression test in \`file-list.test.ts\` that creates a 150k-file subtree and asserts \`listPathsRecursively\` returns instead of throwing; confirmed it reproduces the exact \`RangeError\` against the current code and passes with the fix.

labels.description: Host daemon, process lifecycle, memory, event loop

title: File listing crashes with 502 on large workspaces (Maximum call stack size exceeded)
